title: Feedback, appraisal & your PDP
blurb: Giving and receiving feedback well, getting the most from appraisal, and turning it all into a personal development plan.
question: Your annual appraisal is next week. A colleague has recently told you your notes sometimes miss details, and you'd like to train in radiography one day. What should you bring to the appraisal, and how should the outcome shape your personal development plan?

teach.body: Feedback is information about how you're doing, given close to the event. Appraisal is a regular, structured, two-way meeting with your manager to review your work and agree what to develop next. Your personal development plan (PDP) is the written plan that comes out of it: what you will learn, why and by when. The GDC requires every registrant to keep a PDP as part of Enhanced CPD.

Good feedback is private, prompt and based on specific things you observed, not on someone's personality. Describe what happened, why it matters for patients, and agree a way forward. Asking the person how they think it went first often makes it a conversation rather than a telling-off. When you receive feedback, listen without getting defensive, ask for examples, thank the person and reflect on it. Feedback you act on is one of the best sources for your PDP.

teach.h: Appraisal: a planning meeting, not a telling-off
teach.body: An appraisal is usually held once a year with your line manager. Its main purpose is to identify your development needs and agree objectives. You review how the last year went, discuss feedback, and talk about where you want your career to go, such as training in radiography or moving into management. It is not a disciplinary meeting. You get the most from it by preparing: bring examples of your work, your CPD log and honest reflections on what went well and less well.

teach.body: For the GDC, a PDP must include the CPD you plan to do (relevant to your field of practice), the development outcome each activity links to, and the timeframe for completing it. Build it from reflection on your role, feedback, appraisal and any gaps in your knowledge. If appraisal reveals a weakness, plan CPD that targets it directly. The GDC encourages you to review your PDP annually and adjust it as your role and learning needs change.

items: Feedback: private, prompt, specific, about observed actions, with a way forward.
Receive feedback openly: listen, ask for examples, thank, reflect, act.
Appraisal: identify development needs and agree objectives; prepare with examples and reflections.
PDP: planned CPD, linked development outcomes, timeframes; review it annually.
Target appraisal weaknesses with specific CPD; plan career moves through appraisal.

summary: You can now give feedback that is private, prompt and specific, receive feedback constructively, prepare for and use appraisal to agree objectives, and build a GDC-compliant personal development plan that targets your real development needs.

A.q: You need to give feedback to a colleague who left a used tray in the surgery. Which approach is best?
options: Mention it in front of the next patient
Raise it privately, soon, with the details
Save it all up for their next annual appraisal
Tell the manager and say nothing to them
A.why: Effective feedback is private, prompt and based on specific observations.

whyNot.0: Public feedback embarrasses the colleague and is unprofessional in front of patients.
whyNot.2: Waiting weeks makes the feedback less useful and lets the problem continue.
whyNot.3: Going straight to the manager skips the chance to resolve it directly.

A.q: What is the main purpose of an appraisal?
options: To decide whether to start disciplinary action
To check the nurse's GDC registration and indemnity
To identify development needs and agree objectives
To set the staff rota for the following year
A.why: Appraisal is a structured, two-way review to identify development needs and agree objectives.

whyNot.0: Appraisal is about development, not discipline.
whyNot.1: Registration and indemnity checks are done separately by the employer; they aren't the purpose of appraisal.
whyNot.3: Rotas are an everyday management task, not the purpose of appraisal.

A.q: Which document records the learning you plan to do over your CPD cycle?
options: Your log of completed CPD activity
Your annual CPD statement
Your job description
Your personal development plan
A.why: The PDP sets out the CPD you plan to do, the outcomes it links to and when.

whyNot.0: The activity log records CPD you have already completed, not what you plan to do.
whyNot.1: The annual statement declares your hours to the GDC; it isn't a plan.
whyNot.2: A job description sets out your duties, not your learning plan.

B.q: You are preparing for your first appraisal. What would make it most useful?
options: Bringing examples of your work and reflections
Waiting to hear what your manager thinks first
Preparing a list of complaints about colleagues
Asking for the meeting to be kept very short
B.why: Examples and honest reflections give the discussion substance and help identify real development needs.

whyNot.1: Appraisal is two-way; arriving unprepared wastes the opportunity.
whyNot.2: Appraisal is about your development, not other people's faults.
whyNot.3: Rushing it means needs and objectives may be missed.

B.q: At appraisal, your manager notes you lack confidence handling impression materials. Which CPD is most appropriate?
options: A general course on dental practice management
Hands-on training with impression materials
An online module on medical emergencies
A lecture on the history of dentistry
B.why: A weakness identified at appraisal is best addressed by CPD that targets it directly.

whyNot.0: Management training doesn't address a clinical skills gap.
whyNot.2: Medical emergencies CPD is important, but it doesn't target this weakness.
whyNot.3: This has no link to the identified need.

B.q: A colleague tells you your notes sometimes miss the local anaesthetic batch number. What is the most professional response?
options: Explain that you're always too busy
Point out mistakes they have made too
Ignore it, as they aren't your manager
Thank them, ask for examples and reflect
B.why: Receiving feedback well means listening, clarifying, thanking the person and reflecting on how to improve.

whyNot.0: Making excuses blocks learning and leaves a record-keeping risk.
whyNot.1: Counter-criticism is defensive and damages teamwork.
whyNot.2: Feedback from any colleague can improve patient safety.

C.q: A dental nurse wants to move into a practice manager role in a few years. What is the most appropriate first step?
options: Discuss it at appraisal and plan the learning
Resign and apply for manager jobs elsewhere
Stop doing any clinical CPD straight away
Wait for the current manager to leave or retire
C.why: Career goals are best discussed at appraisal so the development needed can be planned into the PDP.

whyNot.1: Resigning without a plan or the skills needed is premature.
whyNot.2: While they still work as a dental nurse, their CPD must stay relevant to that field of practice.
whyNot.3: Waiting passively means no development takes place.

C.q: Which approach best informs what goes into your personal development plan?
options: Choosing the cheapest courses available
Copying a colleague's plan to save time
Reflecting on your role, feedback and gaps
Picking topics only in your final year
C.why: A PDP should be built from reflection on your own role, the feedback you've had and gaps in your knowledge.

whyNot.0: Cost isn't a measure of what you need to learn.
whyNot.1: A colleague's needs and field of practice differ from yours.
whyNot.3: CPD should be planned across the whole cycle, not left to the end.

C.q: Under the GDC's Enhanced CPD scheme, what must a PDP include?
options: Your appraisal scores from five years
Planned CPD, outcomes and timeframes
Certificates for every course done
A reflective essay on every patient
C.why: The PDP must set out the CPD you plan to do, the development outcomes linked to each activity, and when you expect to complete it.

whyNot.0: Appraisal scores aren't a GDC requirement for the PDP.
whyNot.2: Certificates are evidence kept in your CPD record, not part of the plan itself.
whyNot.3: Reflection is encouraged, but the GDC doesn't require an essay per patient.

reteach.title: Think like a football coach
reteach.question: A coach gives quick tips during the match, reviews the whole season at the end, then writes next season's training plan. Which of these is feedback, appraisal and the PDP?

blocks.body: The coach's word at half-time is feedback: quick, private and about one specific moment. The end-of-season review is appraisal: a look back at the whole year and an agreement about what to work on. The training plan for next season is the PDP: what you'll practise, why and by when. Each one feeds the next, and the plan gets updated as the new season goes on.

explain.body: Keep it private, prompt and specific. Describe the action you saw and its effect on patients, then agree a next step. Avoid comments about personality.

test.q: Which piece of feedback is most effective?
options: "You never seem to pay any attention in surgery"
"Everyone in the team has noticed your attitude"
"The suction wasn't ready for the 10am patient"
"You really need to try harder from now on"
test.why: It describes a specific, observed action that the person can do something about.

whyNot.0: It's a sweeping criticism of personality, not a specific action.
whyNot.1: It's vague, public in tone and gives nothing to act on.
whyNot.3: It's vague and gives no specific action.

explain.body: Listen, ask for examples, thank the person, reflect and act. Feedback can come from colleagues, patients, audit results and appraisal. The Safe Practitioner Framework expects you to use feedback in your own professional development.

test.q: A patient survey says you seemed rushed when giving post-op advice. What should you do first?
options: Reflect on it and plan how to improve
Assume the patient was having a bad day
Ask the manager to remove the comment
Stop giving post-op advice yourself
test.why: Patient feedback is valuable; reflect on it and plan a change, which can feed into your PDP.

whyNot.1: Dismissing feedback stops you learning from it.
whyNot.3: Giving advice is part of your role; the answer is to improve it.

explain.body: A regular two-way meeting to review the year, identify development needs, agree objectives and discuss career goals. Prepare examples and reflections.

test.q: Which statement about appraisal is correct?
options: It is the first step in a disciplinary process
It only happens when a problem has occurred
Only the manager should speak during it
It is a two-way review to plan development
test.why: Appraisal is a regular, two-way conversation to review performance and plan development.

whyNot.0: Appraisal and discipline are separate processes.
whyNot.1: Appraisal is routine, usually yearly, not a response to problems.
whyNot.2: Your input and reflections are central to it.

explain.body: The GDC requires your PDP to include planned CPD relevant to your field of practice, the development outcomes each links to, and timeframes. Review it annually.

test.q: How often does the GDC encourage you to review your PDP?
options: Only at the end of each 5-year cycle
Once a year (annually)
Only when the GDC requests it
Every time you finish a course
test.why: The GDC encourages registrants to review their plan annually as their role and needs change.

whyNot.0: Waiting five years means the plan goes out of date.
whyNot.2: The PDP is for you; don't wait for the GDC to ask.
whyNot.3: You can update it then, but the GDC's encouragement is an annual review.
